epithet: Why do you say what you do not do?
lede: Some of the Companions sat wishing they knew which deed Allah loves most, so that they could do it. They were told. The surah that answered them opens with a rebuke and closes with an offer: a trade that saves from a painful punishment.

names.name: al-Ṣaff
names.note: From its fourth ayah: Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a rank, as though they were a structure joined firmly.

names.name: al-Ḥawāriyyīn
names.note: A name Ibn al-Jawzī records, after the disciples of ʿĪsā in its last ayah.

revelation.detail: It is Madinan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah and the majority; Ibn Yasār held it Makkan. Its subject — fighting in ranks, and the promise of a victory near at hand — is Madinan, and the man who relates its occasion, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, accepted Islam only after the Hijrah.
revelation.when: Madinah, in the years when fighting had been made a duty

evidence.quote: وَيُقالُ لَها سُورَةُ الحَوارِيِّينَ وَفِيها قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: مَدَنِيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، والجُمْهُورُ. والثّانِي: مَكِّيَّةٌ قالَهُ ابْنُ يَسارٍ
سورة الصف مَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، فِيمَا ذَكَرَ الْمَاوَرْدِيُّ. وَقِيلَ: إِنَّهَا مَكِّيَّةٌ، ذَكَرَهُ النَّحَّاسُ عَنِ ابْنِ عباس. وهي أربع عشرة آية

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «الصَّفِّ» بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «الصَّفِّ» بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās, in another report: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās.

setting: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām relates how it came down. “A group of us, Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, were sitting and talking, and we said: if only we knew which deed is most beloved to Allah, we would do it. Then Allah sent down: ‘All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah… O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?’” And he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us, to the end.

The answer to their wish turned out to be the hardest thing: to stand in the line of battle and not break. And the surah begins by pointing out that it is easier to wish than to do. Other reports the commentators gather say the same from another side — that some had asked for fighting to be prescribed and then hung back when it was.{reported}

Two prophets are then brought as witnesses to what a community can do to its messenger. Mūsā: “My people, why do you hurt me, when you know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?” And ʿĪsā, who came confirming the Torah and giving good news of a messenger to come after him, whose name is Aḥmad — and who was called a sorcerer for it.

It closes by naming the bargain. Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in His cause with your wealth and your lives: He will forgive you and admit you to gardens. “And another thing that you love: help from Allah, and a victory near at hand.”

occasions.title: “If only we knew which deed Allah loves most”
occasions.text: “We sat, a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: if we knew which of the deeds is most beloved to Allah, we would do it. So Allah sent down this surah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us.”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: al-Tirmidhī (3309) and Aḥmad; its chain is ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī.

evidence.quote: ما رَوى أبُو سَلَمَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلامٍ، قالَ: قَعَدْنا نَفَرًا مِن أصْحابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَقُلْنا: لَوْ نَعْلَمُ أيُّ الأعْمالِ أحَبُّ إلى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ؟ عَمِلْناهُ

aim: To rouse the believers to support the religion of Allah and to strive in His cause.
themes: Mūsā and ʿĪsā with their peoples

outline.title: Word and deed
outline.summary: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah. O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? It is most hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do. Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a rank, as though they were a building firmly joined.

outline.title: Two messengers, and a third
outline.summary: Mūsā said: “My people, why do you hurt me?” — and when they swerved, Allah let their hearts swerve. ʿĪsā son of Maryam said: “Children of Israel, I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming the Torah before me and bringing good news of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Aḥmad.” They wish to put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion.

outline.title: The trade
outline.summary: O you who believe, shall I direct you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And another thing you love: help from Allah, and a near victory.

outline.title: Be helpers of Allah
outline.summary: O you who believe, be helpers of Allah — as ʿĪsā son of Maryam said to the disciples, “Who are my helpers towards Allah?” and they said, “We are the helpers of Allah.” A party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved; We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became the ones who prevailed.

keyAyah.why: The question the surah opens with — asked of believers, and meant to be uncomfortable.

virtues.text: “I have names. I am Muḥammad, and I am Aḥmad. I am al-Māḥī, by whom Allah wipes out disbelief. I am al-Ḥāshir, at whose feet the people will be gathered. And I am al-ʿĀqib, the last.”
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this surah to us, to its end. Each narrator in the chain then says the same of the one before him.
virtues.grade: Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī

before: Al-Mumtaḥanah set out whom the believers may not take as allies. Al-Ṣaff sets out what is asked of them in place of talk: to stand together.
after: Al-Ṣaff recalls a people who hurt their prophet and a people who denied theirs. Al-Jumuʿah speaks of those given the Torah who did not carry it — and of the favour done to this community in its Messenger.

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī
